name: CTET Paper 2 (Maths & Science)
fullName: Central Teacher Eligibility Test – Paper II (Elementary Stage, Classes VI–VIII), Mathematics & Science stream
frequency: Usually twice a year (sessions are sometimes skipped or shifted)
approxCandidates: ≈18.7 lakh appeared for Paper 2, both streams combined, in the Feb 2026 session (Papers 1 + 2 together: 26.5 lakh registered, 23.2 lakh appeared)
eligibility: Graduation (50%) plus B.Ed, or Graduation plus a 2-year D.El.Ed, or a 4-year integrated B.A./B.Sc.Ed or B.El.Ed (final-year students may apply), as per NCTE norms. No upper age limit, and the certificate is valid for life.

notification.summary: The September 2026 (22nd) CTET was notified by CBSE around 11 May 2026 and scheduled in offline OMR mode on 6 Sep 2026. Applications are closed and the result is awaited. In the Feb 2026 session, Paper 2 had a pass rate of only 18.56% (3.47 lakh qualified); the result was declared on 30–31 Mar 2026. The next cycle's notification is expected around Nov–Dec 2026. Dates come from news reports found by web search on 2026-10-10, because ctet.nic.in could not be reached from the research sandbox. Verify on the official site.
notification.source: https://ctet.nic.in (official), cross-checked with the CBSE Feb 2026 result notice https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/documents/PUBLIC_%20NOTICE_CTET_Feb_2026_RESULT_31032026.pdf and Careers360/PW news reports

pattern.notes: Real paper: 150 MCQs of 1 mark each, no negative marking, 2½ hours. Qualifying marks are 60% (90/150) for General and 55% (82/150) for SC/ST/OBC/PwD. Officially, 'Mathematics & Science' is a single 60-question section (30 Maths + 30 Science). It is split into two sections here only for analysis. Within each subject, about 20 questions test content (NCERT Classes VI–VIII) and 10 test pedagogy. This mock uses English as Language I and Hindi as Language II, and the languages must differ. The question bank holds 60 original questions (CDP 12, English 10, Hindi 8, Maths 15, Science 15), so a mock built from it is a scaled-down version of the full paper.

trendAnalysis.summary: This analysis covers the Jul 2024, Dec 2024 and Feb 2026 sessions. No CTET exam was held in calendar 2025: the Dec-2025 cycle was conducted on 8 Feb 2026. Paper 2 is consistently tougher than Paper 1, with only 18.56% passing in Feb 2026. The Maths & Science section is the most time-consuming: Maths content leans on geometry (angles, triangles, polygons, symmetry), integers/fractions and simple algebra, while Science content is drawn from NCERT Class VI–VIII topics (materials, the living world, electricity & magnets, light). Pedagogy questions now use classroom scenarios, for example van Hiele levels, error analysis, inquiry-based science and process skills. CDP for Paper 2 emphasises adolescence, Kohlberg, inclusive education (RPwD Act 2016) and NEP-2020 aligned assessment.

resources.notes: CBSE does not keep a public archive of CTET question papers. After each exam it posts the provisional answer key together with each candidate's scanned OMR sheet and question-paper set under 'Candidate Activity' on ctet.nic.in for a short challenge window. Final keys and result notices are published on ctet.nic.in and cbse.gov.in. Full past papers in circulation are reconstructions by coaching publishers, not official copies.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation?
options: A student studies hard to win a cash prize
A student solves extra puzzles because she enjoys the challenge
A student revises only because marks will be displayed on the notice board
A student completes homework to avoid a scolding
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest or enjoyment in the task itself. Prizes, avoiding punishment and public recognition are all external (extrinsic) motivators.

questions.question: According to Vygotsky, children talking aloud to themselves while solving a problem ('private speech'):
options: Should be strictly discouraged in class
Is a sign of a speech disorder
Shows cognitive immaturity and serves no purpose
Helps them guide and regulate their own thinking
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw private speech as a tool for self-regulation that gradually becomes inner speech. Piaget, by contrast, considered egocentric speech to be non-functional.

questions.question: A 13-year-old can reason, "If all metals conduct electricity and X is a metal, then X conducts electricity," and can systematically test hypotheses. According to Piaget, she is in the:
questions.explanation: Abstract, hypothetico-deductive reasoning develops in the formal operational stage (about 11 years onwards).

questions.question: An adolescent says, "We must obey traffic rules because society would collapse into chaos if everyone ignored laws." According to Kohlberg, this reasoning belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Upholding laws to maintain social order is Stage 4 (conventional level). Stage 5 (social contract) sees laws as agreements that can be changed for the greater good.

questions.question: Which statement best describes adolescence?
options: It is marked by a decline in abstract thinking
It is a period of stable and unchanging emotions
It is a period of rapid physical change and a search for identity
It is marked by complete dependence on parents for decisions
questions.explanation: Adolescence brings puberty-related physical changes and, as Erikson described, the crisis of identity versus role confusion.

questions.question: Which is considered the primary agent of socialisation for a child?
questions.explanation: The family is the first and primary agent of socialisation. School, peers and media are secondary agents.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of Robert Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence?
questions.explanation: Sternberg's three components are analytical (componential), creative (experiential) and practical (contextual). Emotional intelligence was popularised by Salovey, Mayer and Goleman.

questions.question: In school-based assessment, a portfolio is:
options: A purposeful collection of a learner's work over time that shows progress
A list of marks arranged in rank order
A record of a learner's attendance
questions.explanation: Portfolios collect samples of a student's work over time and support assessment of growth and reflection.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: Which strategy is most helpful for a student with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)?
options: Give long assignments to keep the student busy
Break tasks into short steps with clear instructions and frequent feedback
Allow no movement or breaks at all
Seat the student near the door and windows
questions.explanation: Short, structured tasks with immediate feedback suit the attention span of learners with ADHD. Seating near distractions makes focusing harder.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: How many types of disabilities are recognised under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016?
questions.explanation: The RPwD Act, 2016 expanded the list of specified disabilities from 7 (in the 1995 Act) to 21.

questions.question: A Class VII science textbook shows only men as scientists. What is the most appropriate response from the teacher?
options: Tell students that science suits boys better
Discuss this with students and introduce examples of women scientists
Ask only girls to read about the scientists
questions.explanation: Questioning gender bias in materials and offering counter-examples builds gender sensitivity.

questions.question: Who emphasised 'learning by doing' and described the school as a miniature society?
questions.explanation: John Dewey, a pioneer of progressive education, advocated experiential learning and schools as democratic miniature societies.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

According to the passage, bamboo does not need to be replanted because:
options: It regenerates from its own roots after harvesting
Builders reuse the same bamboo for many years
It belongs to the tree family
It is naturally resistant to insects
questions.explanation: The passage states that bamboo 'regenerates from its own roots after harvesting', so it does not need to be replanted.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

Which of the following is NOT supported by the passage?
options: Bamboo has been used to build bridges
Engineers are studying bamboo as a substitute for steel
Bamboo belongs to the grass family
questions.explanation: The passage says untreated bamboo is vulnerable to moisture, so the claim that it resists moisture contradicts the passage.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

The word 'vulnerable' in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Vulnerable means exposed to damage or harm. Untreated bamboo is easily damaged by insects and moisture.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"Rain on the tin roof, a drummer at night,
Knocking and rolling till morning's first light;
The frogs in the ditches sing loud as they please,
And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees."

In the first line, the rain is called 'a drummer at night'. The figure of speech used is:
questions.explanation: The rain is directly identified with a drummer, without 'like' or 'as', so it is a metaphor.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"Rain on the tin roof, a drummer at night,
Knocking and rolling till morning's first light;
The frogs in the ditches sing loud as they please,
And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees."

The line 'And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human ability to tell secrets and whisper, so the line uses personification.

questions.question: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) mainly focuses on:
options: Using language for meaningful communication in real-life situations
Translating texts between English and the mother tongue
Achieving grammatical accuracy through drills alone
Memorising rules of grammar and spelling
questions.explanation: CLT treats communicative competence as the goal and uses tasks such as role-plays and information-gap activities.

questions.question: Many Class VII students make subject–verb agreement errors in their written work. What is the most effective remedial approach?
options: Give focused practice in meaningful writing tasks, with feedback and peer editing
Make students copy the rule ten times
Ignore the errors because they will disappear on their own
Deduct marks for every error without explanation
questions.explanation: Remediation works best when the specific error is addressed in context with feedback, rather than through rote copying or punishment.

questions.question: A rubric for assessing students' paragraph writing should mainly include criteria such as:
options: Content, organisation, vocabulary and grammatical accuracy
questions.explanation: A writing rubric should reflect the components of good writing: ideas, organisation, language use and mechanics.

questions.question: Reading a text quickly to get its general idea or gist is called:
questions.explanation: Skimming is fast reading for the gist. Scanning is searching for specific information such as a date or name.

questions.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms
questions.question: 'Language across the curriculum' implies that:
options: Language learning is the responsibility of the language teacher alone
English should be taught only in the English period
Every subject teacher contributes to the development of students' language
Students' home languages should be kept out of school
questions.explanation: Language develops through all subjects, so every teacher plays a part in building language proficiency.

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

गद्यांश के अनुसार पुस्तकें 'सच्ची मित्र' क्यों हैं?
options: क्योंकि वे केवल मनोरंजन करती हैं
क्योंकि वे बिना स्वार्थ के ज्ञान देती हैं
क्योंकि वे परीक्षा में अंक दिलाती हैं
questions.explanation: गद्यांश में कहा गया है कि पुस्तकें 'बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं', इसलिए वे सच्ची मित्र हैं।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

'स्वार्थ' शब्द का विलोम है —
questions.explanation: स्वार्थ (अपना हित) का विलोम परमार्थ (दूसरों का हित) है। 'स्वहित' स्वार्थ का समानार्थी है।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

'पढ़ने की आदत' में 'की' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.explanation: का, के, की संबंध कारक के चिह्न हैं। कर्म का चिह्न 'को' है, करण का 'से/के द्वारा' है, और अपादान का 'से' (अलग होने के अर्थ में) है।

questions.question: 'माता-पिता' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: माता-पिता = माता और पिता। दोनों पद प्रधान हैं और 'और' का लोप है, अतः यह द्वंद्व समास है।

questions.question: उच्च प्राथमिक स्तर पर 'सुनने' के कौशल का विकास करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त गतिविधि है —
options: कहानी या समाचार सुनाकर उस पर बातचीत और प्रश्न करना
questions.explanation: सुनी हुई सामग्री पर बातचीत और प्रश्नों से ध्यानपूर्वक सुनने और समझने का कौशल विकसित होता है।

questions.question: उच्च प्राथमिक स्तर पर व्याकरण सिखाने का सबसे प्रभावी तरीका है —
options: केवल व्याकरण की पुस्तक के अभ्यास करवाना
भाषा के प्रयोग के संदर्भ में व्याकरण सिखाना
व्याकरण के नियम और परिभाषाएँ रटवाना
व्याकरण को पाठ से अलग, केवल सूत्रों के रूप में पढ़ाना
questions.explanation: व्याकरण संदर्भ में, यानी पाठों और भाषा-प्रयोग के माध्यम से, सिखाने पर अधिक सार्थक और स्थायी होता है।

questions.question: सतत और व्यापक आकलन के संदर्भ में भाषा-आकलन का मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
options: केवल वार्षिक परीक्षा के अंक देना
बच्चों की आपस में तुलना करना
बच्चों को उत्तीर्ण या अनुत्तीर्ण घोषित करना
बच्चों की प्रगति जानकर शिक्षण-प्रक्रिया में सुधार करना
questions.explanation: आकलन का उद्देश्य सीखने में सहायता करना है। उससे मिली जानकारी शिक्षण को बेहतर बनाने में प्रयुक्त होती है।

questions.question: कविता शिक्षण का मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
questions.explanation: कविता शिक्षण का प्रमुख लक्ष्य रसानुभूति, कल्पना और सौंदर्यबोध का विकास है।

questions.question: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
Find the value of (−12) × (−5) ÷ (−4) + 7.
If 3x − 7 = 2x + 5, what is the value of 2x?
questions.explanation: 3x − 2x = 5 + 7 gives x = 12, so 2x = 24.

questions.question: ₹720 is divided between two friends in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 9 and one part = 720 ÷ 9 = 80. Larger share = 5 × 80 = ₹400.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The angles are 2k + 3k + 4k = 180°, so k = 20°. Largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. Each angle = 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.question: A polyhedron has 8 vertices and 12 edges. How many faces does it have?
questions.explanation: Euler's formula: F + V − E = 2, so F = 2 − 8 + 12 = 6. (A cube is an example.)

questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 10 cm and 16 cm, and the distance between them is 7 cm. What is its area?
The volume of a cube is 343 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Edge = ∛343 = 7 cm. Total surface area = 6 × 7² = 294 cm².

questions.question: What is the median of the data 3, 8, 5, 12, 7, 10?
questions.explanation: Arranged in order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. With an even count, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (7 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.5.

questions.question: A Class VI student says, "A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal," but insists that a square cannot be a rectangle. According to the van Hiele model, the student is at the level of:
questions.explanation: At the analysis level, learners describe shapes by their properties but do not yet see relationships between classes of shapes. Seeing that a square is a special rectangle needs informal deduction.

questions.question: A student simplifies 3(x + 4) as 3x + 4. The error shows that the student:
options: Has not correctly applied the distributive property
questions.explanation: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. The student multiplied only the first term inside the bracket, which is a misapplication of the distributive property.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of George Pólya's four steps of problem solving?
options: Carry out the plan → Understand the problem → Devise a plan → Look back
Devise a plan → Understand the problem → Look back → Carry out the plan
Understand the problem → Carry out the plan → Devise a plan → Look back
Understand the problem → Devise a plan → Carry out the plan → Look back
questions.explanation: In How to Solve It, Pólya gives the steps as: understand, plan, execute, then review (look back).

questions.question: Using open-ended questions in mathematics assessment mainly helps a teacher to:
options: Assess students' different strategies and reasoning
Make all students reach the same single answer by the same method
questions.explanation: Open-ended tasks allow several approaches or answers and show how students think.

questions.question: In mathematics, deductive reasoning means:
options: Arriving at specific conclusions logically from accepted axioms or general statements
Making a general rule after observing a few examples
Solving problems only by trial and error
questions.explanation: Deduction moves from the general (axioms, theorems) to the specific. Generalising from examples is inductive reasoning.

questions.question: A food sample is tested with a few drops of dilute iodine solution. Which observation confirms the presence of starch?
options: A translucent patch forms on paper
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black with starch. A violet colour with copper sulphate and caustic soda indicates protein, and a translucent patch indicates fat.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting produces a new substance, iron oxide, so it is a chemical change. The others are physical changes.

questions.question: Turmeric paper turns red when it is dipped in:
questions.explanation: Turmeric is a natural indicator that turns red in basic solutions. Lime water (calcium hydroxide) is basic, lemon juice and vinegar are acidic, and sugar solution is neutral.

questions.question: In which cell organelle does photosynthesis take place?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis. Mitochondria are the site of respiration.

questions.question: In human lungs, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries, and gaseous exchange happens across their thin walls.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by the poliovirus. Typhoid and tuberculosis are bacterial, and malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.

questions.question: An electric fuse works on which effect of electric current?
questions.explanation: When too much current flows, the fuse wire heats up and melts, which breaks the circuit.

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
options: Real, inverted and of the same size as the object
Virtual, erect and of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, laterally inverted image of the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.question: A car covers 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 km ÷ 2.5 h = 60 km/h.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exhaustible natural resource?
questions.explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel that forms over millions of years, so its reserves can be used up. Sunlight, wind and air are inexhaustible.

questions.question: In an inquiry-based science classroom, the teacher should mainly:
options: Give definitions first and ask students to memorise them
Demonstrate every experiment while students copy the results
Encourage students to ask questions, make predictions and test them through investigation
Avoid questions that do not have a single textbook answer
questions.explanation: Inquiry-based learning engages students in questioning, investigating and drawing conclusions from evidence.

questions.question: A student says, "If I give more water to this plant, it will grow taller than the other one." Which science process skill is the student using?
questions.explanation: The student states a testable, tentative explanation of the relationship between two variables. That is a hypothesis.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the nature of scientific knowledge?
options: It is accepted only on the basis of authority
It is tentative and can be revised in the light of new evidence
It is absolute and can never change
It is a fixed collection of facts to be memorised
questions.explanation: Science is a dynamic, evidence-based body of knowledge that is open to revision.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to assess students' practical (laboratory) skills?
options: Observing students as they perform the activity, using a checklist
Checking how neat their practical notebooks look
Asking students to recite the procedure
questions.explanation: Psychomotor skills are best assessed through direct observation of performance against defined criteria.

questions.question: Many students believe that heavier objects always fall faster than lighter ones. What is the most effective way for the teacher to address this misconception?
options: Create cognitive conflict through a demonstration, followed by discussion
Tell students they are wrong and move on
Ask students to memorise the correct statement
Avoid the topic because it confuses students
questions.explanation: Dropping objects of different mass together creates cognitive conflict. When students confront the discrepancy and discuss it, their concepts change.
